claims.text: Machine-learning optimization of SPS heating rate, dwell time, and applied pressure will enable full densification of ceramic or oxide powder compacts at a lower temperature than conventional sintering.
The proposed starting materials are as-produced, unsintered ceramic or oxide powder compacts.
The intervention uses a data-driven machine-learning framework to optimize SPS heating rate, dwell time, and applied pressure.
SPS provides rapid heating and pressure-assisted densification.
Optimized SPS conditions will control grain growth and preserve phase composition.
Previously accumulated experimental and simulation data can be used by a machine-learning model to predict an effective combination of SPS parameters.
The machine-learning-selected SPS parameter combination will accelerate densification.
The machine-learning-selected SPS parameter combination will minimize grain coarsening.
Accelerated densification and minimized grain coarsening will reduce the required sintering temperature while maintaining material properties.
Optimized SPS will achieve near-full densification comparable to conventional sintering at a lower sintering temperature.
Optimized SPS will avoid excessive grain growth and undesirable phase transitions.
Conventional high-temperature sintering can yield full densification but often increases grain growth and may form secondary phases.
The approach is applicable to ceramic or oxide powders amenable to mechanical activation and SPS processing.
The approach may not work for materials that do not respond to rapid heating or that have substantially different diffusion kinetics.
The magnitude of the sintering-temperature reduction will vary with material composition.
